title: Cientista de Dados Sênior
description:
Atividades

Liderar projetos de ciência de dados de ponta a ponta, desde a definição do problema até a implementação de modelos em produção;

Extrair, processar, limpar e analisar grandes volumes de dados estruturados e não estruturados;

Desenvolver e implementar modelos preditivos e algoritmos de machine learning para resolver problemas de negócios.

Identificar padrões, tendências e oportunidades através de análises exploratórias de dados.

Criar e otimizar modelos de machine learning (supervisionado, não supervisionado, aprendizado por reforço) para solucionar problemas de negócios, como previsão de demanda, classificação de clientes, detecção de fraudes, entre outros.

Explorar novos algoritmos e metodologias de aprendizado profundo (deep learning) para aplicações avançadas, como processamento de linguagem natural (NLP), visão computacional e reconhecimento de padrões.

Monitorar o desempenho dos modelos após a implementação em ambiente de produção, ajustando-os conforme necessário para garantir que continuem otimizados à medida que novos dados se tornam disponíveis.

Desenvolver relatórios e dashboards interativos, utilizando ferramentas de visualização de dados (Tableau, Power BI, D3.js, Matplotlib, Seaborn), para comunicar os resultados de maneira clara e intuitiva.

Garantir que os projetos de ciência de dados sigam todas as regulamentações de proteção de dados, privacidade e segurança, como LGPD (Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados) ou GDPR.

Requisitos

Formação superior em Ciência de Dados, Estatística, Matemática, Computação, Engenharia ou áreas correlatas

Experiência mínima de 3 anos como cientista de dados, com foco em machine learning e análise de dados.

Forte habilidade em programação, com proficiência em linguagens como Python, R e SQL.

Requisitos

Estudos
Ensino Superior

Cocriar e estruturar propostas comerciais sob medida, desenvolvendo internamente novos formatos de modelos de negócio, contratos e precificação, alinhados às particularidades de cada parceiro estratégico;

Liderar negociações estratégicas complexas, envolvendo múltiplos stakeholders e ciclos de venda mais longos, garantindo sustentabilidade financeira e ganho mútuo;

Atuar na ativação estratégica dos canais, definindo planos comerciais, metas, governança e indicadores de performance para garantir escala e consistência de vendas;

title: Shipping Coordinator
description:
The Shipping Coordinator is primarily responsible for the fulfillment of products according to incoming sales orders. Increasing responsibilities of the position include order management, order fulfillment scheduling, inventory management and METRC/LeafLink inventory management.

Reports to: Fulfillment Operations Manager


Position Duties & Responsibilities (included but not limited to):

  • Prepare and check orders according to SOPs
  • Print and review invoices, manifests and pick lists against prepared orders
  • Create transfer manifests and pick lists in METRC/LeafLink
  • Review sales orders in LeafLink for accuracy
  • Organization of finished goods inventory according to product type
  • Complete inventory audits against various inventory management software
  • Prioritize order preparation according to customer location and pickup/delivery dates
  • Support and resolve any packaging/fulfillment issues once orders have been received by the customer


Competencies & Qualifications:

  • Have a high level of attention to detail
  • Be self-motivated with the ability to prioritize
  • Enjoy working both autonomously and in a team environment
  • Excellent time and task management skills
  • Previous experience in METRC, LeafLink, and/or other inventory management software, a plus
  • Warehouse and/or manufacturing experience a plus
  • Cannabis experience is desirable but not required
  • Must possess or qualify for a MED Key or Support Badge


Physical Demands:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to:

  • Regularly standing, bending, and reaching during the employee’s scheduled shift
  • Lifting 50lbs at a time


Compensation & Benefits:

  • Compensation Range: $20.00/hr to $21.00/hr (depending on experience)
  • Medical, Dental and Vision Health Benefits
  • Voluntary Life Insurance
  • 401(K)
  • Up to 48 hours of paid sick leave
  • Up to 40 hours of paid vacation
  • Paid holidays
  • 1 personal day per year of completed employment (max of 5 days)
  • Dispensary Perks (includes discounted product & merchandise)

title: Lead Operations Tech
description:
The Lead Operations Tech works hands-on alongside the Operations team while taking ownership of METRC and the administrative side of Operations. This role keeps compliance records accurate and in shared systems, supports the Operations Manager with day-to-day coordination, and helps train and guide Operations Techs, ensuring continuity, efficiency, and compliance with all regulatory and SOP requirements throughout the facility.

Reports to: Operations Manager


Required Schedule:

Tuesday - Saturday, 6:00 a.m. - 3:00 p.m. MST

OR

Tuesday - Saturday, 2:00 p.m. - 11:00 p.m. MST


Position Duties & Responsibilities (included but not limited to):

Lead Responsibilities: METRC & Administrative Support

  • Own METRC entries for Operations, including package creation, transfers, adjustments, waste and reconciliation, keeping records accurate and audit ready.
  • Maintain Operations administrative records (batch sheets, manifests, inventory counts and logs) in shared systems so information is accessible to the whole team.
  • Support the Operations Manager with daily task coordination, workflow tracking and scheduling.
  • Train and guide Operations Techs on SOPs, compliance and documentation standards, and serve as a point of contact when the Operations Manager is unavailable.
  • Partner with the Quality department on controlled documents and compliance documentation.


Production & Packaging

  • Execute all production, packaging, and labeling processes across product types.
  • Operate production and packaging equipment (cartridge filling, heat-sealing, RadSource, etc.).
  • Complete and review batch sheets with accuracy.
  • Perform quality assurance and quality control on all finished products.
  • Conduct inventory counts, reporting, and organization of packaged goods.
  • Maintain cleanliness and sanitation across all production and packaging areas.


Cultivation & Plant Care

  • Maintain plant health in all growth stages (mothers, clones, veg, bloom).
  • Water, feed, prune, top, and manage plants according to cultivation schedules.
  • Take clones, and ensure proper labeling and compliance.


Harvest & Trim

  • Harvest plants efficiently, including defanning, hanging, and wet/dry processing.
  • Perform dry trimming, de-boning, and strain-specific trimming techniques with speed and accuracy.
  • Maintain proper labeling, strain tracking, and batch organization to prevent mislabeling.
  • Serve as quality control on the trim floor, ensuring accuracy and productivity of 3rd-party trim crews.
  • Assist with cleaning, packaging, and HVAC/filter maintenance on non-harvest days.


Compliance, Safety & Facility Operations

  • Maintain warehouse compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, and SOPs.
  • Follow all security procedures and ensure secure handling of plants and products.
  • Track plant waste and assist with regulatory compliance documentation.
  • Maintain cleanliness and organization throughout all facility areas (veg, bloom, prep, trim, dry, cure, exterior).
  • Support cross-facility operations when needed and work all scheduled shifts.


Retail Operations & Customer Service

  • Verify ID and ensure only approved individuals (21+ or medical patients) enter beyond the front desk; maintain accurate visitor logs.
  • Present a professional, customer-focused demeanor while communicating daily specials, promotions, and product information.
  • Answer phones with proper etiquette, assist with customer inquiries, and route messages to leadership as needed.
  • Stay knowledgeable on all product pricing, promotions, medical vs. recreational menus, and cannabis product details (cannabinoids, terpenes, effects, brands).
  • Perform administrative tasks such as filing, scanning, printing, shredding, and maintaining organized records.
  • Support storefront presentation through cleanliness, organization, and general housekeeping tasks.
  • Deliver exceptional customer service, creating a friendly and welcoming retail environment.
  • Assist leadership with product intake, restocking, barcode accuracy, and inventory rotation.
  • Communicate daily deals, specials, and expiring inventory to staff; report discrepancies immediately.
  • Support compliance by assisting Budtenders with transactions, checking in visitors, updating METRC records, uploading sales, and labeling new product.
  • Maintain accurate filing of manifests, invoices, patient files, and closing documents; complete all opening/closing duties per SOP.


Competencies & Qualifications:

  • Reliable work attendance required
  • Enjoy working both autonomously and in a team environment
  • Be self-motivated with the ability to prioritize
  • Excellent time and task management skills
  • Packaging and/or manufacturing experience a plus
  • Cannabis experience is desirable but not required
  • Have a high level of attention to detail
  • Must possess or qualify for a MED Key or Support Badge
  • METRC experience and strong administrative and record-keeping skills preferred


Physical Demands:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to:

  • Lift and/or move more than 50 pounds
  • Standing for multiple hours
  • Twisting, bending and complete range of motion movement.


Compensation & Benefits:

  • Compensation Range: $22.00/hr to $23.00/hr (depending on experience).
  • Medical, Dental and Vision Health Benefits
  • Voluntary Life Insurance
  • 401(K)
  • Up to 48 hours of paid sick leave
  • Up to 40 hours of paid vacation
  • Paid holidays
  • Personal Days (based on longevity with the company)
  • Dispensary Perks (includes discounted product & merchandise)

title: SBA Business Development Officer
description:
Summary The SBA Business Development Officer is a producing, revenue-generating role responsible for originating, structuring, and closing SBA 7(a) loans, SBA 504 loans, and other SBA and conventional commercial loans for small and mid-sized businesses throughout Locality Bank’s South Florida market. In addition to loan production, the officer brings in the full banking relationship, including commercial deposits and treasury management services, to increase the overall profitability of the Bank. The officer also serves as Locality Bank’s SBA subject-matter expert, partnering with the Commercial Banking team to identify SBA opportunities within the existing client base, and represents Locality Bank in the community through active participation in business, professional, and civic organizations.

Bank Culture

Locality Bank is a community bank with an innovative spirit. We empower local businesses to maximize their potential through personalized banking solutions, deep relationships, and forward-thinking financial technology. The bank’s culture blends inspiring innovative ideas, ownership, trust and authenticity with the warmth of a community bank. We believe a successful, local, banking relationship brings business success too.

Role Overview

This is an individual-contributor position reporting to the EVP / Chief Revenue Officer. The SBA Business Development Officer owns the SBA lending relationship from first contact through closing and funding, working side by side with the bank’s SBA Operations Team (processing, underwriting, and closing), the Credit Department, and CDC partners (for SBA 504 transactions). The role blends outbound business development with hands-on credit structuring, so the ideal candidate is equally comfortable calling on referral sources and business owners as they are analyzing financial statements and SBA eligibility. Locality Bank offers a collaborative, entrepreneurial environment where officers are encouraged to bring new ideas, take ownership of their results, and build long-term relationships in the community.


What Success Looks Like in This Role

  • Consistently generates a healthy, well-qualified pipeline of SBA 7(a) and 504 opportunities from referral sources, centers of influence, and the Bank’s Commercial Banking team.
  • a fast, clear, and professional experience for borrowers, from initial discovery call through closing and funding.
  • Structures sound, SBA-compliant loans that are approved efficiently and perform well over time.
  • Cross-sells deposit and treasury management solutions so that SBA borrowers become full-relationship clients of Locality Bank.
  • Becomes a recognized, trusted SBA resource within the Bank and across the South Florida business and professional community.


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Business Development & Loan Origination

  • Proactively prospects, develops, and converts new SBA and commercial lending opportunities, including leads from Centers of Influence (CPAs, attorneys, business brokers, commercial real estate professionals, and other referral partners), secures appointments, and closes sales opportunities.
  • Works closely with the Commercial Banking team to source deals from internal partners, conducts regular training on SBA programs and SBA SOP requirements, joins commercial lenders on sales calls, and performs the follow-up necessary to secure strong SBA lending opportunities.
  • Develops a thorough understanding of the Bank’s SBA offerings, including the SBA 7(a) Loan, 7(a) Small Loan, International Trade Loan, CAPLines, and the SBA 504 Loan, and is able to explain program eligibility, terms, uses of proceeds, and guaranty fees to prospects and referral partners in plain language.
  • Interviews applicants to determine financing needs and gathers the information required for SBA loan applications.
  • Promotes the Bank’s deposit and treasury management products to SBA clients and prospects to establish full banking relationships.
  • Documents prospecting activity, pipeline status, and client interactions in the Bank’s CRM system and reports pipeline and production regularly to management.


Credit Analysis, Structuring & Underwriting

  • Analyzes each applicant’s financial condition, credit history, cash flow, collateral, and asset values to determine the feasibility of the request, and establishes an appropriate loan amount and credit limit through written and/or oral assessment.
  • Determines eligibility and the potential for an SBA guaranty in accordance with the current SBA SOP 50 10 (Lender and Development Company Loan Programs) and related SBA policy and procedural notices.
  • Structures loans within Locality Bank’s loan policy and SBA requirements, and champions loan opportunities to the Credit Department and/or Loan Committee for proper approval.
  • Resolves open questions on application information through follow-up with applicants, creditors, and other third parties.
  • Works in tandem with the Bank’s SBA Operations Team to process, underwrite, and close each SBA 7(a) loan.
  • Partners with the Bank’s CDC partners to process, underwrite, and close SBA 504 loans.


Closing, Portfolio & Relationship Management

  • Prepares and presents the financing proposal and term sheet to the applicant consistent with credit approval.
  • Reviews loan documentation prior to closing for completeness and acceptance by the applicant, and ensures timely loan closing and funding.
  • Maintains positive, active working relationships with customers, Bank staff, local professionals, and Centers of Influence to expand the customer base and build long-term relationships.
  • Assists in managing the loan portfolio, including renewals, modifications, updated credit analysis, collections, and portfolio monitoring.
  • Studies and evaluates new markets, programs, policies, and services related to business development, and recommends new products based on identifiable customer needs.
  • Community Engagement, Compliance & Other Duties
  • Participates in networking events and in community and professional organizations where membership or involvement will enhance the profitable growth of the Bank and its visibility in the market.
  • Works closely with the Bank’s Advisory Boards to provide products and services to the community.
  • Attends management and staff meetings, as well as sales, pipeline, and credit meetings as required.
  • Assures compliance with established Bank policies and procedures and with SBA requirements.
  • Complies with regulatory requirements and Bank policies and procedures for BSA/AML/CFT compliance.
  • Uses experience and sound judgment to plan and accomplish goals.
  • Performs all other duties and responsibilities as assigned.


Key Performance Measures

  • Annual SBA loan production (number and dollar volume of SBA 7(a) and 504 loans closed), measured against goals set annually with the EVP / Chief Revenue Officer.
  • Quality and size of the SBA pipeline, including new opportunities sourced and conversion rates.
  • Commercial deposit and treasury management relationships generated from SBA clients.
  • Loan credit quality, documentation accuracy, and compliance with Bank policy and SBA requirements.
  • Referral partner development, internal training provided, and community involvement.


Education and Qualifications Requirements

  • High School Diploma or equivalent required
  • Bachelor’s Degree in Business Administration, Finance, or a related area preferred
  • Minimum five years’ experience in small business lending, with experience in marketing, sales, finance, or a related field
  • Demonstrated experience originating and structuring SBA 7(a) loans; SBA 504 experience preferred
  • Training in SBA lending and the SBA SOP 50 10 requirements
  • Proven record of business development and loan production, with an established network of referral sources in South Florida preferred
  • Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation for local business travel

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Knowledge of the banking industry, including business development, sales, and marketing
  • Working knowledge of SBA 7(a) and 504 program requirements, eligibility, and SBA SOP 50 10, and of the Bank’s products and services
  • Knowledge of local, state, and federal regulations governing the banking industry
  • Skill in prospecting, networking, and consultative selling
  • Skill in financial statement, tax return, cash flow, and collateral analysis
  • Skill in communicating with employees, customers, and referral partners
  • Ability to exercise good judgment in establishing and maintaining working relationships
  • Ability to handle stressful situations, solve problems, and deliver a high level of accuracy, focus, and timeliness with limited supervision
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality
  • Ability to work in an organized manner and manage multiple deals and deadlines simultaneously
  • Ability to read, analyze, and interpret policies, contracts, credit and financial documents, and other legal documents as needed
  • Ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with employees, customers, the Board of Directors, and the public


Competencies

  • Proficient with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) and other financial software; comfortable using a CRM to manage pipeline and client activity
  • Understands the capabilities of the Bank’s core software applications and Information Technology protocols
  • Relationship builder with a strong sales drive, self-motivation, and a sense of ownership for results
  • Sound credit judgment, attention to detail, and the integrity to uphold Bank and SBA compliance standards
  • Collaborative team player who partners well with lenders, underwriters, operations, and credit staff
